Context

OneTap Vendor and the SU app form a backbone of everyday campus life at BITS Pilani, supporting more than US$1.2 million in annual campus purchases. We built the campus credit system from scratch for campus eateries. Students use a QR in the SU app, vendors scan it, and purchases are linked to the student's mess account. The balance is billed at the end of the semester.

A credit system from the ground up

The core workflow connects a student's identity, the vendor's bill, and the student's mess account. This lets students make campus purchases on credit and settle those charges through semester-end mess billing.

THE CAMPUS CREDIT FLOW

Student's SU app QR→Vendor scans & records purchase→Student mess account→Semester-end bill
Our own campus credit system connects the SU app, vendor application, and mess-account billing.

Implementation

I worked on the desktop application in Go and Fyne, with SQLite for local transaction storage and sqlc for compile-time type-safe database access. Automatic backups support operational recovery.

Offline synchronization

Unreliable connectivity should not stop a queue or lose a recorded purchase. I built an offline-first synchronization engine with retries and exponential backoff so locally recorded transactions can synchronize reliably when connectivity returns.

Outcome

The platform supports 5,000+ students across campus eateries and $1.2M+ in annual campus purchase volume, with charges connected to student mess accounts for semester-end billing.
